# XAMPP keeps showing Dashboard/Welcome Page instead of the Configuration Page

Upgrading from an older version of XAMPP to a newer release introduces a significant shift in how you access the administration interface. Previously, navigating to `127.0.0.1` or clicking the Apache admin button directed traffic to a legacy configuration wizard featuring language selection and system checks. In modern iterations of XAMPP, specifically versions like 5.6.x and later, that default endpoint now serves as a static "Welcome" or dashboard page. This change can be disorienting for developers accustomed to the older setup, leading to the assumption that an installation has failed simply because the configuration wizard is missing.

The core issue here is not a botched install, but rather a deliberate architectural decision by the XAMPP team. The old configuration interface was often clunky and prone to errors across different environments. The new dashboard replaces it with a cleaner, PHP-based landing page designed to guide users toward setting up their environment through a more robust mechanism. However, this transition breaks backward compatibility for scripts that attempt to call the legacy admin endpoints directly.

When you visit `http://localhost/xampp/`, seeing an empty directory listing confirms that your server is serving files correctly from the `htdocs` or default directory. The "missing" configuration page isn't gone; it has been replaced by the new welcome screen logic embedded in the web root. If you are trying to access the old setup wizard, you will find it inaccessible because the underlying PHP script responsible for that specific legacy view has been deprecated or removed in favor of the new dashboard logic.

To regain control over your environment, you must bypass the automated welcome page and configure XAMPP manually. The most reliable method involves accessing the core configuration file directly via FTP or a local file editor. Navigate to your XAMPP installation directory (typically `C:\xampp` on Windows) and open the `httpd.conf` file located in the `apache\conf\extra` folder.

Inside this file, look for the line defining the server root:
```apache
DocumentRoot "C:/xampp/apache/htdocs"
```
Ensure that the path is correct for your specific installation. If you are running into permission issues or the new dashboard preventing access to admin tools, you may need to explicitly disable the default index file handling that triggers the welcome page. You can do this by adding a `DirectoryIndex` directive at the top of your `httpd.conf`:
```apache
<Directory "C:/xampp/apache/htdocs">
    Options Indexes FollowSymLinks MultiViews
    AllowOverride None
    Require all granted
</Directory>

# Disable default index files to prevent welcome page auto-load if needed
DirectoryIndex index.html index.php
```
While the new dashboard is generally safer, forcing access to the legacy configuration tools requires specific steps. If your goal is strictly to configure Apache modules or virtual hosts without using the GUI, you can disable the `mod_rewrite` module temporarily or comment out the relevant lines in `httpd.conf` if they are intercepting requests meant for the admin panel.

It is also worth noting that the "Admin" button in the XAMPP Control Panel has been updated to link directly to these new PHP-based endpoints rather than the legacy CGI scripts. If your workflow depends on the old orange-yellow configuration screen, you are effectively locked out of it in newer versions. The solution is to accept the new interface or manually edit the `httpd.conf` to point to specific custom admin pages if you have developed them.

For those moving to a production environment where XAMPP is no longer recommended due to its "all-in-one" nature, consider transitioning to a dedicated web server like Nginx or Apache on a Linux distribution, paired with a separate PHP runtime. This separation of concerns provides better security isolation and makes managing configuration pages significantly more predictable. If you are building a Laravel application locally using XAMPP, ensure your `.env` file points to the correct `APP_URL` to avoid confusion between the local dashboard and your application root.
